summary: A double-resonator coupler (DRC) for transmons is proposed: two resonators joined by a single Josephson junction and a capacitor, whose common and differential modes give two exchange paths between the qubits that interfere. Flux-tuning the differential mode cancels ZZ completely at the idle point for detunings well outside the straddling regime, and near half a flux quantum gives $|\mathrm{ZZ}| \approx 70$ MHz, enough for a 20 ns CZ gate with simulated coherent infidelity below $10^{-5}$ and fidelity above 99.9% once relaxation and flux noise are included.
motivation: Tunable couplers have brought two-qubit fidelities close to 99.9%, but cancelling residual ZZ usually restricts the qubit-qubit detuning to the straddling regime or relies on a direct qubit-qubit capacitance. Both constrain frequency allocation and qubit placement.
method: The differential mode behaves as a flux-tunable rf-SQUID and the common mode as a fixed oscillator; sweeping the differential mode through the common mode changes the relative strength of the two virtual exchange paths and takes the effective coupling from positive through zero to negative. The CZ gate is a round-trip baseband flux pulse from the idle point towards half a flux quantum, shaped as a Slepian-like three-term Fourier series and optimized in full-Hamiltonian simulations (qubit detuning 590 MHz, anharmonicities $-200$ MHz).
result: ZZ crosses zero at the idle flux even with no direct qubit-qubit capacitance, and the zero is insensitive to the Josephson energy of the coupler junction; at 20 ns the coherent infidelity is about $10^{-5}$, 74% of it leakage. With $T_1 = 50$ µs on all qubit and coupler modes relaxation adds $3\times10^{-4}$, and $1/f$ flux noise of $(1\,\mu\Phi_0)^2/\mathrm{Hz}$ at 1 Hz adds $1.6\times10^{-5}$, so the gate stays above 99.9% and is relaxation-limited, which asks for coupler modes near 8 GHz with $Q \approx 10^6$.
